overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation as alleged: counsel's drafting and circulation of findings and members' individual review were permissible, and the Board need not discuss matters in depth. It did not formally decide the August 28 executive session, though it flagged serious concerns, including that attorney-client privilege is not a basis for executive session.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly deliberated on draft findings of fact and conclusions of law outside a posted meeting, before the September 25 vote, via counsel's drafts and member correspondence.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find that counsel permissibly drafted and distributed the findings of fact and conclusions of law to Board members prior to the September 25 meeting; Board members individually reviewed the draft as well as supporting materials

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to substantively discuss the findings at the September 25 meeting before voting, because it had already deliberated privately beforehand.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to discuss any matter, nor to discuss a matter in any particular depth.

allegations.summary: Concern raised by the AG, not a complaint allegation: the August 28 executive session with counsel relied on attorney-client privilege and an improper Purpose 7 citation.
allegations.key_passage: Because the propriety of the Board's August 28 executive session was not adequately and timely raised in a complaint filed with the Board, we do not formally determine whether the August 28 executive session was held in accordance with the Open Meeting Law.
